overview: The Western Han established the model of Confucian bureaucratic government that would dominate China for two millennia. During this period, China became a major Eurasian power, connected to Central Asia and the Mediterranean through the Silk Road.

items.text: Cai Lun presents improved papermaking techniques to the court, using bark, hemp and rags.
Zhang Heng invents the first seismograph, a bronze vessel that detected earthquake directions.
Zhang Qian sets out for the west, opening the Silk Road trade routes.
The wheelbarrow appears in Han China, revolutionizing transport of goods.
Blast furnaces and cupola furnaces improve iron production for tools and weapons.
The Records of the Grand Historian by Sima Qian establishes the standard form of Chinese dynastic history.
Calligraphy becomes a refined art with brush and ink on silk and paper.
Emperor Wu establishes Confucianism as state orthodoxy, founding the Imperial Academy.
Buddhism enters China via Central Asian trade routes.
Silk exported to Central Asia, India, Persia and the Roman Empire.
Horses, grapes, alfalfa and other goods imported from the Western Regions.

fall.text: Wang Mang, a regent and relative of the imperial family, usurped the throne and established the Xin dynasty in 9 CE.
